text: Any returned value numerically equal to the largest prime factor is acceptable, e.g. the float 29.0 or a numpy integer (no return type is annotated in the signature).
For n <= 1, which has no prime factor, the function must signal the error by raising an exception.
For prime n the largest prime factor is still well defined (n itself), so the function must return n; the assumption only tells the implementer that this case need not be handled specially.
